Framed by inflation-forecast targeting and the New Keynesian Phillips curve, the FOMC’s June 2018 statement—solid growth, strong labor market, and inflation near the symmetric 2% objective—supports gradual rate increases consistent with Taylor-rule guidance. However, the April 2018 SLOOS points to some incremental tightening and mixed demand in credit intermediation: banks reported tighter credit policies for commercial real estate, wider loan rate spreads, and generally unchanged residential mortgage standards (e.g., qualified jumbo) alongside softer demand in some categories, while foreign banks reported borrower inquiries and demand in CRE and C&I. These SLOOS signals suggest credit conditions were not broadly easing and could modestly temper the pace at which strength transmits to spending and investment via credit channels. Netting the macro strength with SLOOS’s mild tightening/mixed demand tilt, the tone remains positive but more cautious than a purely macro read.
